idiom: bite off more than you can chew
meaning: to take on a task that is too big or too difficult to manage
example: He agreed to run three projects alone, and now he has bitten off more than he can chew.
origin: The image is of taking a mouthful of food too large to chew; the exact origin of the idiom is uncertain

wrong_meanings.meaning: to eat very slowly at a long dinner
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom is figurative and refers to overcommitting to work, not to the speed of eating

wrong_meanings.meaning: to lose a tooth while eating something hard
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has no connection with physical injury or dental problems

wrong_meanings.meaning: to refuse a second helping of food politely
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom describes accepting too much, the opposite of refusing

explanation: 'Bite off more than you can chew' means to take on more responsibility than you can handle. It is often used in workplace conversations when someone has overcommitted.
